This aligns with Bayesian epistemology, wherein new evidence updates beliefs only when it contradicts current models. Risk-metric tradeoffs define the operational cost-benefit landscape, while statistical falsification ensures that proposed edges are not merely coincidental patterns but robust signals. The process mirrors a dual optimization problem: minimizing false negatives (missing true edges) and false positives (false discoveries), constrained by computational and legal boundaries. The breakdown regime occurs when assumptions about data independence or model stationarity are violated, leading to invalid conclusions.
